FACT_ID: sec17-R01 | anchor: A02
Before a long trip, aim for a normal night of sleep and plan to leave rested rather than already tired. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R02 | anchor: A02
The handbook suggests eating lightly before a long trip because a large meal can make some people sleepy. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R03 | anchor: A02
Plan rest breaks about every hour or whenever needed, allowing enough time to finish the trip safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R04 | anchor: A02
Use a rest stop to get out, walk around and get fresh air. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R05 | anchor: A02
Try to avoid driving late at night during the hours when you normally sleep. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R06 | anchor: A02
Do not drive while sleepy; stop to sleep or, when possible, let another driver take over while you rest. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec17-R07 | anchor: A03
Driving experience does not make drinking alcohol and then driving safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R08 | anchor: A03
Driving after drinking can bring fines, higher insurance costs, loss of the license and jail penalties. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R09 | anchor: A03
Illness or discomfort such as a cold, stiff neck or sore leg can affect driving ability. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R10 | anchor: A03
If you feel unwell and need to travel, the handbook recommends having someone else drive. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R11 | anchor: A03
Strong worry, excitement, fear, anger or low mood can interfere with driving well. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R12 | anchor: A03
If angry or excited, wait until calm before driving; a short walk may help allow time to settle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R13 | anchor: A03
Allow extra trip time so impatience does not encourage speeding or other risky actions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec17-R14 | anchor: A03
Do not let impatience at a train lead to driving around lowered gates or trying to beat the train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0135]
